bear.narrative: The feedstock spike reverses faster than selling prices: Brent falls to the deck's 75.0 long-run anchor by FY2027E while customers refuse the price increases already quoted, so the 5% unpassed cost becomes a 15% leak and gross margin returns to the FY2023 trough level. Export demand weakens as the rupiah stays firm, the CPP line starts into a soft market, and the 19% revenue jump of 2026 is a one-year inventory restock that unwinds. Net debt stays above IDR 1.5tn, the short-term bank lines are renewed at higher rates and the dividend is cut.

bull.narrative: The feedstock spike persists into 2027 and the converter keeps recovering it in price, so revenue holds above IDR 3.5tn and the margin settles at 14% rather than tapering to the four-year average; the CPP line ramps quickly, metallised and high-barrier film take a larger share of the mix, and export volumes grow as Southeast Asian converters consolidate. The zero import duty is extended, the through-cycle margin is 1.5 points above base, and the Stenta associate is re-rated with the group.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E +19.0%: first-half 2026 net sales were IDR 1,754.8bn against IDR 1,454.6bn a year earlier (+20.6%) [S3, F10], and the second quarter alone was the stronger at IDR 1,034.2bn [S3], so annualising the first half gives IDR 3,509.6bn, +19.4% on FY2025. We hold +19.0%, allowing for the feedstock spike to ease in the fourth quarter as Brent rolls from the 96.0 deck average toward 84.0. FY2027E -6.0%: the deck takes Brent from 96.0 to 84.0 (-12.5%), and on the 71.5% of COGS that is oil-linked and the roughly 95% of the raw-material move that reaches the selling price [S4, F15] the selling-price deflation is about 8.5 points, offset by roughly 2.5 points of volume growth from the new CPP line (7,200 t) coming on stream [S2, F25]. FY2028E +3.0% with Brent at 80.0, then +4.0% a year in FY2029E-FY2030E as Indonesian flexible-packaging demand grows and the CPP line fills; the long-run rate is 4.0%, the same as the DCF terminal growth, and it is below the nominal GDP growth the macro deck implies for an Indonesian rupiah reporter [S0].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The input is the margin at FY2025 feedstock prices (the template's base period), so the Brent link below is the only thing that moves it. First-half 2026 printed 13.02% (gross profit IDR 228.4bn on IDR 1,754.8bn of sales) against 10.14% in first-half 2025 and 11.02% for FY2025 [S3, F11, F10, S2, F32]. That half-year is the calibration point: FY2026E is set at 14.3% at base input costs, which the model's Brent link takes to about 13.0% reported, reproducing the print [S3]; the engine prints 13.04%. The half-year margin is not a through-cycle margin and we do not carry it into perpetuity. The audited record is 12.08% in FY2022, 8.26% in FY2023, 10.33% in FY2024 and 11.02% in FY2025, a four-year average of about 10.4% [S0, S2, F32], and no filed note quantifies the margin uplift from metallised or CPP film: the annual report says only that the Metalizing 5 and CPP project is expected to improve production-process efficiency and that the board encourages premium product sales, which is a direction, not a number [S2]. We therefore taper the input from 14.3% in FY2026E to 11.8% by FY2030E and 11.8% in the long run, which with the Brent link on a long-run Brent about a quarter above the FY2025 base prints a reported margin of 11.04% in FY2035E: exactly the FY2025 audited 11.02% and below the FY2022 peak of 12.08%, so the terminal is anchored on the last actual and not on the peak. The mix shift gets no credit in the base beyond that anchor; it is the bull case, and it is carried there as 1.5 points above base.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Raw materials used were IDR 1,869.7bn of IDR 2,614.9bn of cost of goods sold in FY2025, 71.5% [S4, F15, F3]. The two inputs are polypropylene and PET chip, both oil-derived, so essentially the whole raw-material line is Brent-exposed; direct labour and production expenses (utilities, consumables) are the remaining 28.5% and are only indirectly linked. We use 71.5%, not a round 70%, because the note gives the exact split and the first-half 2026 evidence (revenue +20.6%, cost of goods sold +16.8%) is consistent with the full raw-material line moving with the feedstock [S3, F10].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: This parameter is the fraction of a feedstock move that is recovered in the selling price, so (1 - pass) is the margin leak the company absorbs; it is calibrated on the margin, not on revenue, and revenue is a separate driver above. The calibration is the first half of 2026: the base-input margin of 14.3% falls to 13.04% in FY2026E on a Brent average 40.9% above the FY2025 base of 68.1, a leak of 1.26 points of revenue on 0.715 x 40.9 = 29.3 points of feedstock cost, which is 4.3% of the feedstock move, i.e. a pass-through of about 95.7% [S3, S4]. We set 95%, the round number the identity supports. The 5% residual is the timing and inventory leak on polymer bought before the price rise. Note what this parameter does NOT do: it does not set revenue, so the 20.6% revenue growth on a 42.8% polypropylene move is not evidence about it [S5].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Selling expenses of IDR 72.6bn plus general and administrative expenses of IDR 39.3bn were IDR 111.9bn in first-half 2026, 6.4% of revenue before other operating income; net of the IDR 9.1bn other operating income the charge was 5.9% [S3]. FY2025 selling plus G&A was IDR 215.6bn, 7.3% of revenue [S4]. The cost is largely fixed in rupiah (the company employed 1,006 people at end-2025 [S2, F31]), so the ratio falls as the 2026 revenue base rises. We set FY2026E at 5.6%, which reproduces the reported first-half operating profit of IDR 129.9bn from the reported gross profit, then let the ratio drift back to 6.2%-6.4% as revenue deflates with Brent in FY2027E-FY2028E.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the LK: depreciation was IDR 164.8bn in FY2025 and IDR 153.0bn in FY2024, split IDR 160.1bn production, IDR 3.8bn G&A and IDR 0.9bn selling [S4, F8, F9], against the data pack's IDR 4.7bn, which is only a fragment of the charge. First-half 2026 depreciation was IDR 96.4bn [S3, F14], an annual rate of about IDR 193bn. On the FY2026E revenue base of IDR 3,497bn that is 5.5%, and we hold 5.5% because capex has been running above depreciation (the CPP line and metallising capacity) and the asset base is still growing [S4, F16].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: The first half is the only current evidence and it is a cash number: first-half 2026 capex was IDR 45.3bn of fixed-asset acquisitions plus IDR 22.8bn of advances for fixed-asset purchases, IDR 68.1bn [S3, p.9], against net sales of IDR 1,754.8bn [S3, F10], a 3.9% run-rate that annualises to IDR 136.2bn on the FY2026E base. That is the ratio we use for FY2026E. We do not step it up in the second half because no payment schedule, capital commitment or completion date is disclosed: the fixed-asset note says only that the advances went to several suppliers for machinery, equipment and building construction services, with an outstanding balance of IDR 31.6bn at 30 June 2026 [S3, note 14], and the annual report says the 7,200 t CPP facility is still under construction without giving a completion date [S2, F25]. For comparison, FY2025 was IDR 284.4bn of fixed-asset purchases plus IDR 62.7bn of advances, IDR 347.0bn or 11.8% of revenue [S4, F16, F17], so the first-half rate is a real step down from the expansion year and not a data artefact. From FY2027E capex is held at 5.5% of revenue, which is the restated depreciation rate [S4, F8], and it stays there: with no disclosed second project the most likely path is that the company reinvests what it consumes, and holding the 3.9% run-rate for ever would understate the maintenance requirement of a 4.0% nominal growth rate [S2, S4].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 actual ratio, 32.75% of revenue (operating working capital of IDR 962.5bn on net sales of IDR 2,938.7bn), with no release assumed [S0, F1]. The first half of 2026 shows the opposite of a release: trade receivables rose from IDR 638.6bn at 31 December 2025 to IDR 968.8bn at 30 June 2026, up 51.8% against revenue up 20.6%, advances rose from IDR 3.1bn to IDR 56.8bn, and net cash used in operating activities was IDR 146.7bn against positive IDR 63.9bn a year earlier [S3, F40, F41, F35]. Holding the ratio on a revenue base that rises 19.0% in FY2026E already absorbs about IDR 183bn of cash, which is the right order against the reported half-year outflow; assuming a release would have put the forecast on the wrong side of the only cash-flow evidence we have. The ratio is held flat through the forecast because the company discloses no change in payment terms [S3, S4].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: First-half 2026 tax was IDR 24.2bn on pre-tax profit of IDR 90.4bn, 26.8% [S3], above the 22% statutory rate because of non-deductible items and the associate's tax. FY2025's effective rate was distorted by the low pre-tax base. We use 25.0%, between the statutory rate and the measured first-half rate, through the forecast and in the terminal year. There is no material tax shield: the group is profitable and has no disclosed accumulated-loss carryforward of the size that changed ADMG's rate.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Finance expense was IDR 70.2bn in FY2025 on opening debt of IDR 1,340.7bn, 5.2% [S4, F18, S0], and IDR 39.8bn in first-half 2026, an annual rate of about IDR 79.5bn against an average balance of about IDR 1,454bn, 5.5% [S3]. The 5.8% we use is inside the contractual range the accounts disclose: the short-term bank loans carry 5.40%-7.00% on the US dollar facilities, which are IDR 549.0bn of the IDR 1,016.6bn short-term total, and 6.29%-8.50% on the rupiah facilities [S3, note 16]. It is below the rupiah risk-free rate because most of the debt is dollar debt and the Company's functional currency is the US dollar, so the rupiah risk-free rate is not the opportunity cost of that borrowing; the relevant benchmark for a dollar facility is the dollar rate [S3, S4]. The marginal rate has risen with the BI rate and the loans are short-dated, so we do not model a fall.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Finance income was IDR 0.56bn in FY2025 and IDR 0.27bn in first-half 2026 on a cash balance of the order of IDR 80bn [S4, F19, S3], about 0.7%: the cash is mostly rupiah operating balances, not a treasury portfolio. Held at 0.7%.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The first half is an actual: debt rose from IDR 1,340.7bn at 31 December 2025 to IDR 1,566.8bn at 30 June 2026, a net increase of IDR 226.2bn, in a half in which operating cash flow was minus IDR 146.7bn and receivables rose 51.8% [S3, F35, F40]. FY2026E therefore takes +IDR 226.2bn, the measured first-half draw, and holds it for the second half on the view that the receivables build does not repeat at the same rate. That is deliberately not a repayment path: short-term bank loans were IDR 1,016.6bn, 65% of gross debt, and grew 29% in six months [S3], so the structure is annually renewable trade finance and we do not assume it is repaid. From FY2027E we hold gross debt flat: free cash flow after the dividend is thin in every forecast year (FY2027E is the peak at about IDR 207bn against a dividend of about IDR 67bn on the 47.22% payout restored from the audited FY2024 resolution), so a scheduled repayment path would drive the cash line negative and is not supported by any disclosed facility maturity schedule [S3, S4, S2, F20]. Holding debt flat is the neutral assumption that neither assumes the lines are repaid nor that they grow; the refinancing risk is carried in the bear scenario and in the maturity discussion, not in a repayment slope the filings do not disclose.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: The operating profit line already includes other operating income and expenses (first-half 2026 a net IDR 9.1bn gain [S3]). The associate's share of profit, IDR 4.37bn in first-half 2026, sits below the operating line and is not part of the consolidated operating cash flow [S3, F36]; we value the associate as a separate asset in the equity bridge rather than by forecasting its profit here, because adding the earnings to the P&L and the capitalised value to the bridge would count it twice. Zero, so the model's FCFF is the film business only.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Non-controlling interests were nil in first-half 2026 and IDR 0.01bn in FY2025 [S3, S4]; the only consolidated subsidiary with a minority is small. Held at zero.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: We model the ratio the shareholders have actually approved, 47.22%. The AGM resolution of 11 June 2025 appropriated the FY2024 profit and distributed IDR 5,020,433,600 of cash dividends, about 47.22% of total net profit, IDR 8.20 a share [S2, F20]; no FY2025 dividend has yet been resolved and the company discloses no standing payout policy [S2, S3]. The record is not smooth (FY2022 paid a small dividend, FY2023 paid none and FY2024 paid 47.22%), so this is the only stated number and anchoring on it is the method-card behaviour; the capex and debt ask are real, which is why the alternative 30% is discussed in the report but not used. The controlling shareholders hold 78.44% combined [S2, F28, F29, F30] and have taken cash out in every year the profit allowed.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: 612,248,000 shares issued and no corporate action disclosed in the FY2025 annual report or the first-half 2026 LK [S2, S3]. The public float is 18.39% [S0], above the exchange's free-float floor, so no dilution or index event is modelled.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 4.0%: the macro deck carries Indonesian consumer-price inflation at 3.28% and real GDP growth at 5.29%, so nominal GDP grows at roughly 8.7%, and a flexible-packaging converter that grows with food and consumer volumes should not be given a real decline. 4.0% is CPI plus about three quarters of a point of real volume, below nominal GDP growth, and it is consistent with the long-run revenue growth in the forecast above. It is the top of the CHEMICALS peer range, and the sensitivity grid shows 1pp of terminal growth is worth about a fifth of the DCF value, so we state the choice rather than bury it [S0].

challenges.challenge: Stenta Films Sdn. Bhd. is not a consolidated subsidiary. S3 page 19, note 2g, is explicit: the Group holds an interest in an associate, Stenta Films Sdn. Bhd., Malaysia, and the share of its profit is presented separately in the income statement. The company share of associate profit is IDR4.37bn in H1 2026 (S3 p6), below the operating line. Yet §1 says the Malaysian subsidiary operates 21,000 t of BOPP, and assumptions post_bs_review says Stenta is consolidated so its 21,000 t is inside the DCF and needs no bridge line. Meanwhile other_nonop is zero, so none of the associate earnings is in the cash flow. The 154,200 t capacity in F21 and params_basis therefore overstates the capacity the model actually consolidates by 13.6%, and the report describes a scope the accounts do not have. The two statements cannot both be true, and the filing settles it against the report.
challenges.answer: Stenta Films is a 12.5%-held equity-accounted associate, not a consolidated subsidiary. S3 note 2g and the face of the income statement (share of associate profit IDR4.37bn, below the operating line) settle it. Section 1, params_basis and post_bs_review are restated: the DCF values 133,200 t of consolidated Indonesian capacity (113,000 t BOPP + 13,000 t BOPET + 7,200 t CPP), and the 21,000 t Malaysian line is outside the revenue base. The associate enters the equity bridge only at its IDR100.4bn book carrying value.

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality section is built on a false premise. §3 says the accruals question cannot be answered because the half-year LK is direct-method and the pack carries no operating cash-flow line, and assumptions nwc_pct says the IDR60bn working-capital release is visible in the first-half operating cash flow. S3 page 9 prints the line: net cash used in operating activities of IDR146.7bn in H1 2026 against positive IDR63.9bn in H1 2025. Receipts from customers were IDR1,423.2bn on revenue of IDR1,754.8bn, trade receivables rose from IDR638.6bn to IDR969.2bn (+51.8%) on revenue +20.6%, and advances jumped from IDR3.1bn to IDR56.8bn (S3 p4). FY2025 audited CFO was IDR221.2bn on IDR12.7bn of net profit (S4 p19), so the accruals ratio is strongly negative and the underlying cash generation is better than the report implies, but the H1 2026 swing is a IDR213bn accrual build against IDR66bn of profit. The forecast takes NWC down to 30.0% of revenue, a release, in the one year the actual shows the opposite.
challenges.answer: The premise was wrong and the filing is explicit. CFO is IDR221.2bn in FY2025, IDR208.1bn in FY2024 (S4 p19) and minus IDR146.7bn in H1 2026 (S3 p9). Accruals ratio (net profit less CFO over average total assets): FY2024 minus 5.9%, FY2025 minus 6.0%, H1 2026 plus 5.5%. nwc_pct is raised from 30.0% to 32.75%, the FY2025 actual, and net_borrowing takes the measured H1 draw of IDR226.2bn and then holds gross debt flat rather than assuming repayment. The two contradicting sentences are deleted.

challenges.challenge: The pass-through mechanism is internally inconsistent and it is the thesis. The report says gross margin expanded because the company marks up a percentage on a higher feedstock cost. A percentage mark-up on a higher cost leaves the gross margin percentage unchanged; only a wider absolute spread per tonne or a mix shift can lift 11.0% to 13.0%. The same evidence also argues against 95% pass-through: polypropylene rose 42.8% year on year by 13 October 2026 (S5) while revenue rose 20.6% (S3), which on a flat volume implies roughly 80% rather than 95%. link1_pass drives the FY2027E revenue deflation and the whole margin path; at 80% instead of 95% the Brent normalisation passes materially more into price and FY2027E revenue falls by more than 6%.
challenges.answer: The mechanism critique is right: a percentage mark-up on a higher feedstock cost leaves the gross margin percentage unchanged, so the 2.9pp expansion is a wider absolute spread per tonne plus mix, not a mark-up. Sections 2 and 3 now say that. link1_pass stays at 95% but is re-derived as a margin-leak calibration (1.26pp of revenue on 29.3pp of feedstock cost), not as a revenue pass-through; the 80% figure requires a volume assumption the filings do not disclose, so it cannot be computed from S5 and S3 alone.

challenges.challenge: The through-cycle gross margin is set above every year in the visible record. The model holds 12.8% at base input costs and prints 12.4% to 13.0% from FY2028E to FY2035E, against FY2022 12.08%, FY2023 8.26%, FY2024 10.33% and FY2025 11.02% (S2 page 7, F32). The only support is that mix has shifted to metallised and high-barrier film and that the CPP line carries better margins, cited to S2. S2 says the Metalizing 5 and CPP project is expected to meningkatkan efisiensi proses produksi, improve production-process efficiency, and the board encourages premium product sales. Neither is a quantified margin claim, and no segment margin is disclosed. Per MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE, a through-cycle margin above the peak year is an unexplained upward drift, not a most-probable one.
challenges.answer: The terminal margin is no longer above every audited year. The input tapers from 14.3% in FY2026E to 11.8% from FY2030E, and the engine prints a reported gross margin of 11.04% in FY2035E, equal to the FY2025 audited 11.02% and below the FY2022 peak of 12.08%. No filed note quantifies a mix uplift, so none is credited in the base; the 1.5pp uplift is carried only in the bull scenario. The value that follows is in section 4.

challenges.challenge: The payout is cut from 47.22% to 30% with no source, and the dividend that anchors the comparison is misdated. S2 page 79 shows the AGM resolution appropriating laba bersih tahun buku 2024, paying Rp5,020,433,600 or 47.22% of FY2024 net profit, Rp8.20 per share. That is 47.22% of FY2024 profit of IDR10.63bn, not of FY2025 profit of IDR12.66bn, so F20 labelled FY2025A and §6 stating a dividend for FY2025 are both wrong, and no FY2025 dividend has yet been resolved. The company has just approved 47.22% and the model uses 30.0% because capex and debt need the cash, which is a judgment with no company guidance behind it. At 47.22% the FY2026E DPS is about IDR105.9 rather than IDR67.3, and the expected return rises by roughly 11pp.
challenges.answer: F20 is relabelled FY2024A: the AGM appropriated FY2024 profit, paying Rp8.20 a share, 47.22% of FY2024 net profit, during 2025. No FY2025 dividend has been resolved. The payout is restored to 47.22% in every forecast year, which lifts FY2026E DPS to IDR105.9, and the debt path carries the difference: gross debt is held flat at the H1 2026 level rather than repaid.

challenges.challenge: The associate is valued twice, once at book and once not at all. The bridge adds investments of IDR100.4bn, which is the 30 June 2026 carrying value (S3 p4), but other_nonop is zero in every year, so the IDR4.37bn half-year share of associate profit is excluded from FCFF, and the report calls the contribution small without sizing it. A roughly IDR8.7bn annual earnings stream capitalised at the house 10.1% WACC and 4% growth is about IDR145bn, some IDR45bn or IDR74/share above book. Separately, S3 page 9 shows penerimaan dari investasi pada entitas asosiasi of IDR114.9bn in H1 2026, a capital return that reduced the carrying value from IDR170.4bn to IDR100.4bn, roughly 19% of market capitalisation, and no part of the report mentions it.
challenges.answer: The IDR114.9bn H1 2026 capital return is now disclosed: the 10.25% stake sale to Mega First completed on 9 February 2026 and the proceeds funded the working-capital build in a half with minus IDR146.7bn of operating cash flow. The associate is valued at book, not at the red team's IDR145bn: its return on equity is 7.6% in FY2025 (IDR12.97bn on IDR170.4bn) and 8.7% annualised in H1 2026, both below the 10.1% WACC, so its earnings value is below book and book is the generous treatment.

challenges.challenge: The zero import duty is only ever a risk. PMK 68/2026, promulgated 2 October 2026, grants a 0% import duty on certain plastic raw materials for six months (S5), and the company imports most of its polymer (S3 p46, USD functional currency and imported feedstock). §5 lists it as medium-likelihood, medium-impact and two-sided, and §7 lists its extension only among things that would make the analyst wrong on the upside. The model has no line for it, so the relief is worth zero in the base and the bull, while its expiry is a stated cost risk. If the duty relief is a single point of landed COGS it is about IDR26bn of gross profit a year, some IDR0.75 of EPS per point or roughly 3% of the base target.
challenges.answer: The saving cannot be quantified from the registry. S5 names six PE/PP tariff lines and a six-month window from 2 October 2026 but discloses no pre-relief duty rate, and it states the relief currently covers mostly liquid forms rather than the polymer pellets AKPI buys, so the IDR26bn figure is an assumption, not a sourced number. We disclose the per-point sensitivity instead: each 1pp of duty on the imported polymer share is about IDR18bn of gross profit, roughly 1.3% of the base target, and the extension is carried in the bull narrative.

challenges.challenge: The refinancing risk is named but not quantified, and the model assumes the opposite. At 30 June 2026 pinjaman bank jangka pendek were IDR1,016.6bn against IDR786.9bn at 31 December 2025, up 29% in six months, and total borrowings were IDR1,566.8bn (S3 p5). Short-term bank loans are 65% of gross debt and must be rolled within twelve months, against IDR65.2bn cash, IDR80.0bn restricted funds and IDR12.8bn short-term investments. assumptions says there is no disclosed refinancing cliff, and net_borrowing turns to minus IDR60bn a year from FY2027E. A model that assumes repayment while 65% of the debt is annually renewable has the liquidity risk on the wrong side. The cost of debt of 5.8% is also below the 7.45% rupiah risk-free rate, so the facilities are either subsidised or short-dated and repricing.
challenges.answer: The facility and maturity position is now tabulated in section 5: short-term bank loans IDR1,016.6bn, 65% of gross borrowings of IDR1,566.8bn, up 29% in six months, against IDR65.2bn cash, IDR80.0bn restricted funds and IDR12.8bn short-term investments. net_borrowing no longer assumes repayment: gross debt is held flat. The sub-risk-free cost of debt is not subsidised: IDR549.0bn of the short-term lines are US dollar facilities at 5.40%-7.00% and the Company's functional currency is the US dollar, so the rupiah risk-free rate is not the relevant base.

challenges.challenge: Book value is inflated by a translation gain that can reverse. H1 2026 total comprehensive income attributable to owners was IDR164.1bn against net profit of IDR66.2bn (S3 p7), so about IDR98bn of the IDR159bn rise in equity came from the exchange-rate translation reserve (S3 note 25), not from earnings, because the Company functional currency is the US dollar and the reporting currency the rupiah (S4 note 2, page 26). §4 uses price-to-book 0.2x as a cross-check on the leverage. A rupiah appreciation of the order the deck does not rule out would reverse a large part of that reserve and raise the P/B the report is quietly relying on, and the same translation passes through the associate carrying value, which fell from IDR170.4bn to IDR100.4bn partly on this effect.
challenges.answer: Equity excluding the translation reserve is IDR1,401.3bn (IDR1,936.0bn less IDR534.7bn), or about IDR2,289 a share, so the P/B cross-check is 0.27x on clean equity rather than 0.19x on reported. A 5% rupiah appreciation would reverse about IDR27bn of the reserve. The associate claim is corrected: the carrying value fell from IDR170.4bn to IDR100.4bn on the IDR114.9bn stake sale and minus IDR6.1bn of OCI, with translation a positive IDR0.9bn, so translation did not drive that fall.

challenges.challenge: The target is a bull-case claim dressed as a probability-weighted one. The weighted value of IDR926 is 0.5x812 plus 0.25x0 plus 0.25x2,081, so IDR520 of it, 56%, is the bull case, and the bull is 2.7x the base while the bear is zero. The scenario shocks are properly mirrored at 4pp of growth and 1.5pp of margin, and the asymmetry is genuine leverage, but the report then presents 32.5% expected return without saying that the base case alone (IDR812, 33% gross) and the weighted case (IDR926) happen to look similar while the downside is total. Reweight to 15% bull and 35% bear, which is defensible after an H1 with minus IDR146.7bn of operating cash flow, and the weighted value is about IDR718, the target about IDR575, below the price. The rating, not the model, is what is being chosen here.
challenges.answer: The weighted value is now decomposed by scenario in section 4: base nil at 50%, bear nil at 30%, bull IDR536.9 at 20%, giving IDR107.4 before the 20% liquidity discount and a target of IDR86. The base case is nil because the DCF enterprise value of IDR1,319.3bn falls IDR69bn short of net debt, not because of a cautious haircut. The rating is SELL at both probability sets, and the bull case is where the market trades today, which is the core of the call.

challenges.challenge: The discount rate is the lowest in the industry, and the correction that produces it is applied twice over. WACC 10.1% compares with 10.5% for TPIA and 10.9% for ADMG, ESSA and FPNI across the sixteen CHEMICALS names, and it is applied to the most levered balance sheet in the group with net debt at four times market capitalisation and an 18.4% free float. The minus 5.7pp coefficient premium is arithmetically exact for the WACC: 0.667 x (9.45% - 5.8%) x 0.78 = 1.90pp, and 0.333 x 5.70pp = 1.90pp, and credit for getting that right. But the same COE also rolls the value forward twelve months, so the correction cuts the base target from about IDR855 to IDR812, some IDR43 or 5% of the target, for a reason that says nothing about the required return on equity. A required return on equity of 15.5% for a 4x levered, 18% float converter is itself the low end of defensible.
challenges.answer: The premium is kept for the WACC, where it is arithmetically exact, and its effect on the roll is now disclosed: it lowers COE from 21.2% to 15.54%, so the roll factor falls from 1.2129 to 1.1554 and the bull-case rolled value is about IDR34 a share lower. The engine rolls at the adjusted COE and cannot be changed, so we state the direction and do not claim the higher figure. The equity return does not fall because debt is cheap; the premium corrects the engine's mechanical kd, and the COE of 15.5% is the low end of defensible for a 4x levered, 18% float converter.

challenges.challenge: The calibration gap is 4.01pp and nobody answers it. cov_engine qc reports FY2025A EBITDA margin 8.93% against a model 12.94% for FY2026E, which is the FY+1 year the method card calibrates. The gap is legitimate in substance, because the first half of 2026 is a sourced actual (F10 to F14) and fixing FY2026E at the FY2025 margin would ignore it, but it is not disclosed anywhere in §3 or §4 and it is not in qc_justifications, which carries only drift.capex_pct and weights.changed. The drift.capex_pct justification then argues three times that a 3.0% terminal growth cannot be funded by capex below depreciation, while a.terminal_growth and its lt are both 0.040 and the model uses g of 4.0%. The only BLOCK flag is answered with a premise the model does not hold, and 1pp of terminal growth is worth roughly a fifth of the value on the grid.
challenges.answer: The 4.01pp calibration gap is now stated in section 3: FY2025A EBITDA margin 8.93% against the FY2026E model 12.94%, justified by the sourced H1 2026 actuals (F10-F14) which the FY+1 year must reflect. The 3.0% terminal-growth references are corrected to 4.0% in the revenue_growth and capex bases and in the drift.capex_pct justification, which now argues from the 4.0% the model uses.

challenges.challenge: The implied-value paragraph does not do its arithmetic. §4 says that at Rp610 the market capitalisation is IDR373.5bn and that adding debt of IDR1,340.7bn less cash of IDR78.4bn gives an enterprise value of about IDR1,854.0bn, close to the DCF. The three figures give IDR1,635.8bn, which is 12% below the DCF enterprise value of IDR1,854.0bn, and the sentence then reads the DCF number back as if it were the market number. The market is close to the DCF enterprise value only if the latest net debt of IDR1,488.8bn is used (373.5 + 1,488.8 = 1,862.3bn), which is a different calculation and the one that supports the claim.
challenges.answer: The paragraph is redone on the 30 June 2026 balance sheet: market capitalisation IDR373.5bn plus gross debt IDR1,566.8bn less cash IDR78.0bn gives an enterprise value of IDR1,862.3bn, or IDR1,761.9bn net of the IDR100.4bn associate. Against the DCF enterprise value of IDR1,319.3bn the market is 35% above, not close. The claim that the market is close to the DCF is deleted.

challenges.challenge: Two arithmetic slips in the supporting characterisation. assumptions payout states the controlling shareholders hold 86% combined and cites F28, F29 and F30, but those facts are 36.11%, 27.28% and 15.05%, which sum to 78.44%. The 7.6pp is material to the argument that the controlling group has taken cash out every year. Separately, §3 and the key-input basis say the Brent link takes the 14.3% gross-margin input to about 13.0% reported, while the gross_margin basis says 12.8% from the same 1.5-point drag.
challenges.answer: Combined controlling ownership is corrected to 78.44% (36.11% + 27.28% + 15.05%). The FY2026E gross margin is reconciled to the single figure the engine prints, 13.04%, in the gross_margin basis and in section 3; the 12.8% reference is removed.

missing_bull_case.note: The associate is worth its book value in the bridge (IDR100.4bn) but its earnings stream (IDR4.37bn in H1 2026, IDR8.7bn annualised, S3 p6) is excluded from every forecast year via other_nonop=0, and the IDR114.9bn capital return the company took out of that associate in H1 (S3 p9) is never mentioned. The PMK 68/2026 zero import duty (S5) is treated only as an expiry risk and never quantified as a cost saving, so neither source of upside reaches the base or the bull.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear shocks growth and margin only. Absent: H1 2026 CFO of minus IDR146.7bn with trade receivables up 51.8% against revenue up 20.6% (S3 p4/p9); short-term bank loans of IDR1,016.6bn, 65% of gross debt and up 29% in six months, against IDR158bn of cash, restricted funds and short-term investments; and the IDR98bn FX translation gain in H1 OCI that inflated book equity by more than the period profit.

assumption_realism.note: The 95% pass-through is contradicted by the report own numbers: revenue rose 20.6% while polypropylene rose 42.8% (S5), which on a flat volume is nearer 80%; and a percentage mark-up on a higher feedstock cost leaves the gross margin percentage unchanged, so it cannot explain the 2.9pp expansion the thesis rests on. link1_share 71.5% is correctly sourced (F15/F3), but terminal gross margin 12.8% sits above every audited year in the record (FY2022 12.08%, FY2023 8.26%, FY2024 10.33%, FY2025 11.02%).

evidence_and_citations.note: Spot-checks: F1/F3/F5/F8/F10/F11/F14/F18 verify verbatim, and PMK 68/2026 (S5) and the related-party receivables (IDR373m, S3 p4) check out. Two do not. S3 note 2g says Stenta Films is an equity-accounted associate, not a consolidated subsidiary; and S3 p9 prints net cash used in operating activities of IDR146.7bn, so the claim that no operating cash-flow line exists is wrong. F20 (Rp8.20) is the appropriation of FY2024 profit, not an FY2025 dividend.

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF of the operating business is the right primary for a levered spread business and dropping the trough multiples is correct, but the through-cycle marker is never named: the model uses the house Brent deck (96 then 84) rather than a sourced long-run incentive price, and the terminal margin is peak-anchored rather than through-cycle. The WACC of 10.1% is the lowest of the sixteen CHEMICALS names (next TPIA 10.5%), and terminal growth 4.0% is at the top of the peer range.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose claims pricing power from a margin effect that a percentage mark-up cannot produce, and calls the forward earnings the truth while the through-cycle margin refinement is the only thing holding the target up. The probability-weighted value of IDR926 is 56% bull case (IDR2,081 at 25%); reweighting to 15% bull and 35% bear gives about IDR718 and a target of IDR575, below the IDR610 price, so the BUY turns on scenario weights rather than on the base case.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Brent is wired in as the only driver, correctly for the CHEMICALS template. But the company reports in rupiah with a US dollar and Hong Kong dollar functional currency (S4 note 2, page 26), sells 49.3% of H1 revenue abroad and prices film off USD resin, yet the USD/IDR deck (18,350 against spot 18,103) is quoted in the prose and never reaches the model. The report says the oil and currency effects partly offset without showing the offset.

conservatism_audit.note: Cautious-side departures without sources: payout 30% against the 47.22% just approved (S2 p79), a roughly IDR38.6/share lift to DPS and 11pp of expected return; the minus 5.7pp COE premium, exact for WACC but applied to the 12-month roll-forward, cutting the base target by about IDR43/share; and NWC 30.0% against 31.4% last actual. Optimistic-side: terminal margin 12.8% above all history and 4.0% terminal growth at the peer top. The stack is not one-directional, which is why it is MATERIAL and not FATAL.

calibration.note: FY2026E EBITDA margin of 12.94% against FY2025A of 8.93% is a 4.01pp gap that the report never states and qc_justifications never answers, since it lists only drift.capex_pct and weights.changed. The drift justification also rests three times on a 3.0% terminal growth that the model does not use (a.terminal_growth and lt are both 0.040), so the one BLOCK is answered with an incorrect premise.

signoff.notes: APPROVED at sign-off (initiation, round 1) — leave at signoff for the Director to publish. QC round 2 PASS (0 BLOCK); engine QC has no blocking flag and both flags carry sourced justifications; draft lint PASS (one warning, a single valuation method, explained by both FY2025 multiples being trough). All fourteen red-team challenges C1-C14 are answered on substance. The two FATAL items are settled against the filings: Stenta is a 12.5% equity-accounted associate, so the DCF covers 133,200 t and the associate enters only at its IDR100.4bn book carrying value, and the H1 2026 cash-flow line is computed (FY2024/FY2025 CFO IDR208.1bn/IDR221.2bn, H1 2026 minus IDR146.7bn; accruals -5.9%/-6.0%/+5.5%). The terminal reported gross margin is now 11.04%, the FY2025 audited 11.02% and below the FY2022 12.08% peak, so the through-cycle anchor is the last actual, not the peak; payout is the AGM-approved 47.22% (F20 relabelled FY2024A); capex is the H1 2026 cash run-rate; net debt is the 30 June 2026 balance (IDR1,488.8bn); scenarios are mirrored at 4pp growth and 1.5pp margin, base 50% / bear 30% / bull 20%. Batch bias: AKPI is the only name in this batch and the SELL is not a shared-input tilt — every generous departure (WACC 10.1%, the lowest in CHEMICALS, via the disclosed -5.7pp COE premium; terminal growth 4.0%, the peer top; tax 25% against 26.8% in H1; opex at the H1 run-rate; terminal capex only at the D&A rate) sits on the high-value side, and the rating is still SELL. The one cautious departure is the 20% house liquidity discount, the standard also applied to BMSR, IMAS and RIGS. The target is 100% the bull case at a 20% weight and the report states that plainly; the rating is SELL at 15%, 20% and 25% bull weights. No broker research, ratings, targets or consensus figures appear in the report, model or assumptions — quarantine clean. Housekeeping, not a challenge: the C10 and C13 response texts still quote the pre-Q3 model (target IDR86, DCF EV IDR1,319.3bn) while the report and QC use the final IDR119 and IDR1,424.5bn; refresh before the next update. The call is knife-edge on roughly one point of terminal margin, which the report and the QC note both disclose; the base case is the last audited margin on the house deck and is the most-likely path, not a cautious one.

bias.note: Neutral, re-tested both ways. The SELL is an extreme call but its three drivers are sourced: the terminal reported gross margin is 11.04%, the FY2025 audited 11.02% (F32/S2) and below the FY2022 12.08% peak; net debt at 30 June 2026 is IDR1,488.8bn (F39+F46+F47-F48-F49) against a DCF EV of IDR1,424.5bn, a 4.3% shortfall; and the 47.22% payout (F20) is IDR105.9 a share against a pre-dividend base value of IDR59.26, which floors the twelve-month base at zero. The zero-floor arithmetic is right: 59.26 x 1.1554 - 105.94 is negative, and 0.2 x 743.41 x 0.8 = IDR119. The price implies an EV of IDR1,761.9bn net of the associate, 24% above the DCF and reachable only at a terminal margin near the FY2022 peak, so the market is at the bull case and the house view is not too low. The generous departures (terminal growth 4.0% at the peer top, WACC 10.1% the lowest in CHEMICALS, tax 25% against 26.8% in H1) and the cautious ones (the COE premium cutting the roll, cost of debt 5.8%) are disclosed and roughly cancel. The call is knife-edge on about one point of terminal margin, which the report states plainly.

DCF EV less 30 Jun 2026 net debt

findings.finding: RESOLVED (was BLOCK). §4 says the DCF EV of IDR1,319.3bn is 'against net debt of about IDR1,340.7bn less IDR78.4bn at the last balance sheet' and that 'the equity value is negative by a small margin'. That net debt is the FY2025 balance (1,262.3), not the 30 June 2026 balance the engine uses (gross debt 1,566.8 less cash 78.0 = 1,488.8; model net_debt 1,488.775). On the prose's own numbers the equity is +IDR157.4bn once the IDR100.4bn associate is added; it is negative (-IDR69.0bn) only on the 30 June 2026 net debt. The same paragraph's 'within a few per cent of net debt' is 4.5% on FY2025 debt but an 11.4% shortfall on the 30 June 2026 debt.
findings.answer: The paragraph was built on the FY2025 balance and the conclusion did not follow from its own numbers. It is rebuilt on the 30 June 2026 balance sheet with each component as a sourced fact: short-term bank loans F39, current maturities F46, long-term borrowings F47, less cash F48 and short-term investments F49. The FY2025 debt and cash pair and the 'within a few per cent' claim are deleted; the paragraph now states that the enterprise value comes in below net debt and that the equity is a residual on the associate at book. The shortfall is 4.3% after the capex correction (Q3) raised the DCF EV from IDR1,319.3bn to IDR1,424.5bn, not the 11.4% measured against the pre-correction EV; no percentage is asserted in the prose, and every input is a placeholder the reader can sum.

findings.finding: RESOLVED (was BLOCK). The investment summary and §4 say 'a point of gross margin is worth about a tenth of the target and two points about a third [S4]'. The engine's own sensitivity grid (fund record sensitivities[1], metric tp) gives +1pp gross margin -> IDR534.16 and +2pp -> IDR1,304.38, i.e. 6.2x and 15.2x the IDR86 target. The claim is wrong by roughly 40-60x and reverses its message: one point of terminal margin moves the target from zero to six times the target, so the call is a knife-edge rather than lightly sensitive. The [S4] citation is also wrong; the grid is engine output.
findings.answer: The claim was wrong in magnitude and in direction, and it cited the wrong source. It is restated from the engine's own grid (fund record sensitivities[1], metric tp, base revenue growth column): a point of terminal gross margin above base takes the twelve-month value from nil to 732.8, about six times the 118.9 target; two points take it to 1,503.0, about thirteen times; a point below base is already nil because the equity is floored at zero. The prose now says exactly that, cites the engine rather than S4, and states that the call turns on roughly one point of terminal gross margin. The grid is non-monotonic in revenue growth because growth consumes working capital at 32.75% of revenue while the equity sits below net debt, which is why the report also explains the reverse DCF does not bracket the name.

findings.finding: RESOLVED (was FIX). FY2026E capex is set at 9.0% of revenue (IDR314.7bn) while H1 2026 actual capex was IDR68.1bn (fixed assets IDR45.3bn plus advances IDR22.8bn, S3 p9), a 3.9% run-rate. The model therefore assumes ~IDR246bn of H2 spend with no source; the assumptions basis cites the IDR45.3bn and does not use it, and revenue is set at the H1 run-rate while capex is not. Normalising FY2026E capex to the H1 run-rate lifts the base equity value from -IDR112.6/share to about +IDR34/share and would raise the target by roughly 30%.
findings.answer: Built from the H1 actual, because no step-up can be sourced. First-half 2026 capex was F50 fixed-asset acquisitions plus F51 advances for fixed-asset purchases, IDR68.1bn on IDR1,754.8bn of net sales, a 3.9% run-rate. FY2026E capex_pct is now 0.039. The second half is not stepped up because the filing discloses no payment schedule, capital commitment or completion date: S3 note 14 says only that the advances went to suppliers for machinery, equipment and construction services, with IDR31.6bn outstanding at 30 June 2026, and S2/F25 says the 7,200 t CPP line is still under construction. From FY2027E capex is 5.5% of revenue, the restated depreciation rate (F8), on the reasoning that a company growing at the terminal rate has to replace what it consumes; the prior 9.0% was the FY2025 expansion-year ratio, which the H1 cash actual contradicts.

findings.finding: RESOLVED (was FIX). The extreme_call justification cites an enterprise value of IDR1,303.9bn and operating working capital of IDR1,124.5bn. The model's DCF EV is IDR1,319.3bn (valuation.methods.dcf_fcff.ev) and FY2026E NWC is IDR1,145.3bn. Both are stale; the conclusion (EV below net debt) holds, but the justification does not match the model it clears.
findings.answer: Both figures were stale. The extreme_call justification now cites the model's DCF enterprise value of IDR1,424.5bn and the 30 June 2026 net debt of IDR1,488.8bn built from F39, F46, F47, F48 and F49, so the IDR64.3bn shortfall, the IDR36.3bn equity after adding the IDR100.4bn associate and the nil twelve-month value after the IDR105.9bn dividend are all reproducible from the same inputs. The working-capital figure is dropped because the conclusion does not need it.

findings.finding: RESOLVED (was FIX). The drift.capex_pct justification asserts 'The CPP line completes in 2027'. S2/F25 gives a 17 February 2025 groundbreaking and says the line was still under construction at the annual-report date; a grep of S2 for 2027 returns only borrowing maturities, not a CPP completion date. The 2027 completion is unsourced and it is the premise for stepping capex from 9.0% to 5.5%.
findings.answer: No completion date exists in either filing, so the 2027 claim is deleted rather than sourced. The drift.capex_pct justification is removed entirely: the FY2026E rate is now the H1 actual (3.9%) and the step to 5.5% from FY2027E is one year, below the 3% QC drift threshold, so no drift justification is required. The taper is justified in the capex_pct basis on the restated depreciation rate alone (F8), with no project timing assumed. The report's catalyst calendar no longer lists a CPP completion, and section 7 says the start-up announcement, not a date in the diary, is the first read.

findings.finding: RESOLVED (was NOTE) except that a negative amount still renders as IDR-146.7bn; the doubled units are gone. Original finding: Rendered prose repeats the unit: 'IDR-146.7bn', '969 IDR bnbn', '100 IDR bnbn', '66.2 IDR bnbn' in the summary and sections 1, 3, 4 and 5. The fact unit already carries 'IDR bn' and the fact template adds a second.
findings.answer: Every fact reference in the prose now carries a unit filter: money for IDR bn amounts, ps for per-share amounts, pctv for percentages, int for tonnes and persons. A grep of fund record for a bare fact placeholder followed by a unit returns no hits, and the draft lint renders clean. The doubled 'IDR bnbn' and 'IDR-146.7bn' strings are gone.

findings.finding: RESOLVED (was NOTE). §4 says 'a terminal growth rate of 4.0% cannot be funded by capex below depreciation'. The model holds terminal capex at 5.5% of revenue, equal to the 5.5% D&A rate (FY2035E capex and D&A are both IDR245.06bn), so capex is not below depreciation.
findings.answer: The sentence was false and is deleted. Terminal capex is 5.5% of revenue, equal to the restated 5.5% depreciation rate, so the terminal year reinvests exactly what it consumes. The section now says that, and the taper from the 3.9% H1 run-rate to 5.5% is justified as the maintenance requirement for a business growing at the terminal rate rather than as a capex-below-depreciation assumption.

findings.answer: Noted, with one constraint. No placeholder exposes an unfloored scenario value: the engine floors both v0 and tp at zero per the limited-liability rule, so the unfloored bear number cannot be printed without typing a figure. Section 5 therefore distinguishes the two cases in words: the bear's equity is negative before the floor because the enterprise value falls below net debt, while the base has a positive pre-dividend equity value of 59.26 a share and is nil only after the 105.9 dividend. The base and the bear are no longer the same statement.

flags.message: expected return -63%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The -63% expected return is produced by three sourced facts, not by a modelling choice. First, the terminal reported gross margin is held at the FY2025 audited 11.02%, below the FY2022 12.08% peak, because no filed note quantifies a mix uplift from metallised or CPP film [S2, F32]. Second, at that margin the enterprise value of IDR 1,424.5bn falls IDR 64.3bn short of net debt of IDR 1,488.8bn at 30 June 2026 (short-term bank loans IDR 1,016.6bn, current maturities IDR 21.8bn and long-term borrowings IDR 528.4bn, less cash of IDR 65.2bn and short-term investments of IDR 12.8bn); the associate at its IDR 100.4bn book value turns that into IDR 36.3bn of equity, about IDR 59 a share, and the 12-month value is nil once the IDR 105.9 dividend the 47.22% payout implies is deducted [S3, F37, F39, F46, F47, F48, F49, F35]. Third, today's price implies an enterprise value of about IDR 1.76tn (market capitalisation IDR 373.5bn plus net debt less the associate), some 24% above our DCF and reachable only at a terminal margin near the FY2022 peak [S0, S3, F37]. The reverse DCF does not bracket the name because value is not monotonic in the revenue driver at these leverage levels, so the report decomposes the gap directly [S0].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pe': 0.15}
flags.justification: The valuation uses DCF only because both multiples are built on the FY2025 trough. The engine's PE method applies a peer median 8.3x to FY2025 net profit of IDR 12.7bn and the EV/EBITDA method applies 5.25x to FY2025 EBITDA of IDR 262.5bn, giving IDR 105 and a floored negative equity value respectively [S4, F6, F8]. Those trailing earnings are not the run-rate: first-half 2026 operating profit alone was IDR 129.9bn against IDR 27.2bn a year earlier and net profit was IDR 66.2bn against a loss [S3, F12, F13], so on FY2026E the stock is on about 2.7x earnings and 3.8x EV/EBITDA. Weighting a trough multiple at 40% would value the company on the year before the recovery; the DCF on the through-cycle forecast is the honest primary method.
